findings.statement: Declared household resources and reported income loss help describe food-insufficiency responses relative to prevalence-only prediction.

reliability.rationale: March-to-May reference Brier0.060243 improves prevalence0.063749 but loses to flexible0.059176. Partial association support and unsupported hinge superiority are therefore appropriate.

mechanism.rationale: Resource proxies and overlapping self-report recall windows do not identify causal income effects. The fixed log-resource hinge is an imposed modeling scale, not a discovered household threshold.

novelty.rationale: Known source analyses and standard mathematical/statistical families are disclosed. This review does not certify a new law or exhaustive novelty.

significance.rationale: A useful weighted cross-wave association benchmark with a strong comparator and explicit complete-case limits.

impact.rationale: No independent deployed intervention, measured cost benefit or external experimental replication establishes industrial impact.
